projectDesc.p: James Joyce's unpublished correspondence, collected, annotated, and made available as a digital edition

div.p: There is no cheque-book at 42. Here are 1 or 2 points of the revise:
Spy – you ought to say perhaps that after some time since his arrival in Z’ch – J.J. was under the Austrian spy system’s observation and surely the stupidest spies are employed by a bewildered State.

Passages by heart: also from A. J. Balfour and Edgard Quinet , the latter is the one I (P.L.) have heard most frequently – it occurs 4 or 5 times in Wip. with all kind of embroidery & variations. I enclose it. The one from Balfour was a pessimistic passage from his Foundations of Belief.
Sullivan : you ought to cancel the name “John” – he is a Paris Opera titulaire and it is against the rules of that theatre to prefix a man-singer’s Christian name – They are simply M.—
Mme St. Leger as she is still living you had better word the allusion to her very carefully though J.J. does not suppose she cares a zap one way or the other.
Another is the attention paid to Joyce’s movements by Austrian spies.
His perspective was probably falsified by the attention paid to him by
P. 34 Austrian Spies had paid him a good deal of attention in his early days in Zch
But Had he backed a system as did we he would the backer would have lost just the same

p.hi: He should have backed a system as did we He

This paragraph has been overwritten in pencil: “Done”. See JJMU 34 for its inclusion.

Balfour and Quinet are mentioned in JJMU 181. The quotation from Quinet (“Aujourd'hui comme aux temps le Pline…”) appears most straightforwardly at FW 281.4-13 and, in part, well over a dozen times elsewhere in the book. Balfour's The Foundations of Belief (London: Longmans, Green, 1895) is referred to several times in FW. The paragraph was overwritten in pencil: “Done”.
Sullivan is duly identified as "M. Sullivan" in JJMU 137. The paragraph was overwritten in pencil: “Done”.
Budgen did not mention Baroness St. Leger by name, but he did write about the “Lady of the Lake” (JJMU 247) – see JJ to Budgen, 17 July 1933 (LI 336).
The following three lines are in ink in Budgen's handwriting.
Budgen is experimenting with sentences that appear in the published book (JJMU 34).
The remaining lines are in pencil in Budgen's handwriting.

JJMU 130. This revised sentence is an example of the minor differences in Budgen's text between the American edition of 1934 (New York: Harrison Smith and Robert Haas) and the English edition of 1934 (London: Grayson & Grayson), which were typeset independently, the London edition incorporating some minor changes. The original sentence as given in Budgen's discussion of the “Wandering Rocks” episode of Ulysses read “Lyons might have followed our system with the same debit result” (128). In accordance with these pencilled notes, showing Budgen experimenting with the wording, the English edition revised this to “Backing a system as we did he would have lost just the same” (130).
Bantam Lyons had bet on one of the losing horses in the Ascot race in Ulysses.
